summary: The ustaz tells two pivotal events of the early Meccan phase: the conversions of Hamzah RA and Umar al-Khattab RA. After the Quraysh envoys returned from Abyssinia in embarrassment, the pressure on the Prophet ﷺ rose and Abu Jahal began to target him directly. Hamzah, who had known the Prophet ﷺ since childhood, struck Abu Jahal in anger that he had been insulted and then accepted Islam. Three days later Umar, who set out with a sword, was moved by the Quran at his sister Fatimah's house before declaring the shahada at Dar al-Arqam. The ustaz ends with lessons on praying for people of potential, not despairing of Allah's mercy, and starting our effort with ourselves and our families.
keyPoints: The Prophet's ﷺ strategy of sending companions to Abyssinia was carefully planned, with representatives of about fifteen tribes.
Rising pressure on an ever smaller Muslim community strengthened the bonds between them.
Hamzah RA accepted Islam unplanned, in anger that Abu Jahal had insulted his nephew, and that night prayed for Allah to show him the truth.
Umar RA changed on hearing Surah Al-Haqqah and reading Surah Ta-Ha at his sister's home, after being told his own family's affair was unsettled.
Umar's conversion made the Muslims feel strong and able to pray openly at the Kaaba, according to Ibn Mas'ud.
Even the person who seems furthest from Islam can change, so we should pray for such people and not despair.

chapters.title: Umar comes with a sword
chapters.summary: The lecture opens at Dar al-Arqam as the companions tremble to see Umar arrive armed, and Hamzah calms them.

chapters.title: Opening and concern for children
chapters.summary: The ustaz gives thanks and voices concern about the challenges of raising and protecting children, and mentions the book The Prophet Also Played.

chapters.title: The hadith on character and three disliked traits
chapters.summary: The Tirmidhi hadith says those closest to the Prophet ﷺ are the best in character, and warns against talking too much, boasting and speaking arrogantly.

chapters.title: A turning point in the Meccan phase
chapters.summary: The ustaz introduces the two stories as a turning point, then tells of the Quraysh envoys returning from Abyssinia in embarrassment.

chapters.title: The Prophet's ﷺ strategy of sending companions to Abyssinia
chapters.summary: Choosing about a hundred people from many tribes eased the pressure and made it hard for the Quraysh to act, since every tribe had treaties and a right to object.

chapters.title: Surah An-Najm that stirred the Quraysh
chapters.summary: The ustaz links the surah to the Quraysh's interest in stars and to the moment they all prostrated when the Prophet ﷺ recited it.

chapters.title: Breaking down tribal walls
chapters.summary: In Abyssinia the companions began to see themselves as Meccans, and in Mecca the small Muslim community grew closer under pressure.

chapters.title: Abu Jahal raises the pressure
chapters.summary: Abu Jahal threatened the Prophet ﷺ directly, and the Muslim hadith tells how he backed away in fear while the Prophet ﷺ was in prostration.

chapters.title: Who was Hamzah ibn Abdul Muttalib
chapters.summary: The ustaz introduces Hamzah as an uncle of the same age as, and close to, the Prophet ﷺ, a private hunter who was respected and had not yet accepted Islam.

chapters.title: Hamzah's anger, striking Abu Jahal and accepting Islam
chapters.summary: After being told that Abu Jahal had insulted the Prophet ﷺ, Hamzah struck Abu Jahal, prayed that night and accepted Islam the next morning.

chapters.title: Umar before Islam
chapters.summary: Umar grew up with a harsh father, could read and write, loved poetry and was a gifted diplomat, and was Abu Jahal's protege.

chapters.title: Umar hears Surah Al-Haqqah at the Kaaba
chapters.summary: One night Umar slipped behind the Kaaba's covering and was struck by the Prophet ﷺ reciting Surah Al-Haqqah.

chapters.title: Umar sets out with a sword and meets Nu'aym
chapters.summary: Umar walked out to kill the Prophet ﷺ, but Nu'aym told him to sort out his own family first, since his sister had already accepted Islam.

chapters.title: Fatimah's house and Surah Ta-Ha
chapters.summary: Umar struck his sister and brother-in-law, was moved by his sister's blood, then read Surah Ta-Ha up to verse fourteen and asked where the Prophet ﷺ was.

chapters.title: Dar al-Arqam and Umar's conversion
chapters.summary: Umar arrived at Dar al-Arqam, the Prophet ﷺ gripped his collar and Umar declared the shahada. The Muslims went out to pray openly and Umar announced his Islam.

chapters.title: The effect and the lessons
chapters.summary: The ustaz sums up the effect of Umar's conversion, Umar as caliph remembering where he came from, and the call not to despair and to start with the family.

One of the main sources for the better-known report of Umar's conversion.

people.role: Uncle and companion of the Prophet ﷺ
people.context: A private, respected hunter of the same age as the Prophet ﷺ, he accepted Islam after striking Abu Jahal for insulting him, then guarded the door at Dar al-Arqam.
Originally a harsh opponent of Islam who had been trained by Abu Jahal, he accepted Islam after hearing the Quran and was called Al-Faruq.

people.role: Quraysh leader and opponent of the Prophet ﷺ
people.context: Called Abu al-Hakam by the Meccans, a shrewd planner of pressure against Islam, and Umar's mentor.
Protected the Prophet ﷺ but did not accept Islam.
Hated the Prophet ﷺ and did not accept Islam.
Accepted Islam rather late compared with Hamzah.
Accepted Islam through the Prophet's ﷺ da'wah without ever meeting him, and protected the Muslims in Abyssinia.
Returned to Mecca without achieving his goal and is said to have been gloomy with shame.

people.role: A Muslim who hid his Islam
people.context: Told Umar, who set out with a sword, to check his own family, because his sister had already accepted Islam.
Had accepted Islam and learned the Quran at home, and was struck by Umar until she bled before he was moved.
One of the ten promised Paradise, son of Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, he was struck by Umar at his house.
Taught Fatimah and Sa'id privately, hid when Umar came, and later showed the location of Dar al-Arqam.
Opposed sacrifice to idols, was tortured by Khattab, and prayed that his son would meet the Prophet ﷺ.
A harsh father who abused Umar in childhood, and also tortured Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl.

people.role: The quickest person in Mecca to spread news
people.context: Umar went to him to announce his Islam, and he ran to the Kaaba to broadcast it.
Stopped the crowd from continuing to beat Umar after he declared Islam.
Narrated the effect of Umar's conversion, that the Muslims were strong and honoured and could pray openly at the Kaaba.
Narrated that Jibril came down conveying the joy of the people of heaven at Umar's conversion.

people.role: Son of an enemy of the Prophet ﷺ
people.context: Spat toward the Prophet ﷺ and was prayed against by him, and was later eaten by a lion on the road. The ustaz says son of Abu Jahal, but the sirah sources usually say son of Abu Lahab, so this needs checking.

lessons.title: Look at yourself and family before pointing fingers
lessons.body: Society's problems are complex. Before blaming others, examine yourself and your own family first.

lessons.title: Hold your tongue and your emotions
lessons.body: Social media algorithms encourage emotion and opinion without thought, so we need to hold our tongue and our emotions.

lessons.title: Children need enough play
lessons.body: Play builds connection, safety and a sense of being loved between children and their parents.

lessons.title: The Prophet ﷺ planned carefully
lessons.body: Every step of the Prophet ﷺ was intentional, including choosing companions from many tribes to migrate to Abyssinia.

lessons.title: Shared pressure strengthens brotherhood
lessons.body: When numbers shrink and the mission is the same, the bond between Muslims grows closer beyond tribe.

lessons.title: Guidance can come unplanned
lessons.body: Hamzah did not plan to accept Islam, but Allah opened his heart when he stood up for his nephew.

lessons.title: Never assume someone cannot change
lessons.body: No one expected Umar to accept Islam, yet he became a great figure of the ummah.

lessons.title: A Quran taken to heart touches the heart
lessons.body: Umar began to feel faith enter his heart when he heard a verse that seemed to answer his thoughts.

lessons.title: Settle your own household's affairs
lessons.body: While Umar was busy with a great cause, he was reminded that his own sister had already accepted Islam.

lessons.title: Work to reach people of potential
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for specific people, so we too should have someone we pray for and befriend if they could change the situation.

lessons.title: Be brave in showing the truth
lessons.body: Umar asked why they should hide if they were on the truth, and then made his Islam public.

lessons.title: Remember where we came from
lessons.body: As caliph, Umar remembered his days as a shepherd and his father's harshness to keep himself humble and not proud.

lessons.title: Do not despair of Allah's mercy
lessons.body: Every good person has a past and every bad person has a future.

lessons.title: Do not wait for a saviour, start with your family
lessons.body: The ustaz rejects the attitude of waiting for a saviour and urges everyone to do what they can, starting with their own family.

glossary.meaning: The secret house where the Prophet ﷺ taught the companions, whose location was never discovered until the Hijra.
An Arab tribe or clan, the basis of bonds and treaties in Meccan society.
The brotherhood of Muslims that cuts across race and tribe.
A person who held to the upright religion of Ibrahim AS, like Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl.
Someone who leaves a religion. Umar used it from the Quraysh viewpoint of the Prophet ﷺ, whom they saw as abandoning the religion and culture of the ancestors.
Sheets on which the Quran was written before it was gathered in one volume.
The title the Prophet ﷺ gave Umar because he distinguished truth from falsehood by making his Islam public.
The title of the leader of the Muslims, such as Umar as caliph.

dalil.context: The ustaz reads it as a reminder about holding the tongue, especially on social media.
dalil.translation: The one I love most and who will be nearest to me on the Day of Judgement is the best of you in character. The one I dislike most and who will be farthest from me is the one who talks a great deal without knowledge, who boasts in his speech and who is arrogant in speech.

dalil.context: Surah An-Najm begins with the star, and the Quraysh were very familiar with stars in their daily talk. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: By the star when it sets!

dalil.context: A sahih hadith showing Allah's protection of the Prophet ﷺ as the Quraysh's pressure rose.
dalil.translation: Abu Jahal asked whether Muhammad prayed in front of the Kaaba, and swore he would tread on his neck. When he approached the Prophet ﷺ in prostration, he backed away and said he saw a trench of fire and wings. The Prophet ﷺ said that if he had taken one more step, the angels would have torn him apart.

dalil.context: The verse that answered Umar's thought that the recitation was poetry, saying it is not the speech of a poet.
dalil.translation: not the words of a poet- how little you believe!-

dalil.context: The next verse denies that the Quran is the speech of a soothsayer, so that Umar felt his mind was being read. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: nor the words of a soothsayer- how little you reflect!

dalil.context: The Quran is a revelation from the Lord of all worlds. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: This [Quran] is a message sent down from the Lord of the Worlds:

dalil.context: If Muhammad had invented some sayings in Allah's name, Allah would have seized him. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: if [the Prophet] had attributed some fabrication to Us,

dalil.context: Allah's warning to cut the vein of his neck had he invented anything, as proof that the revelation is true. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: and cut off his lifeblood,

dalil.context: The Quran was not sent down to make the Prophet ﷺ suffer, an opening verse Umar read. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: It was not to distress you [Prophet] that We sent down the Quran to you,

dalil.context: The Quran is a reminder for those who fear Allah. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: but as a reminder for those who hold God in awe,

dalil.context: The Quran is sent down by the one who created the earth and the high heavens. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: a revelation from the One who created the earth and the high heaven,

dalil.context: Ar-Rahman, who is established on the Throne. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: the Lord of Mercy, established on the throne.

dalil.context: To Allah belongs all that is in the heavens, on earth, between them and beneath the soil. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Everything in the heavens and on earth, everything between them, everything beneath the soil, belongs to Him.

dalil.context: Allah knows what is secret and what is more hidden, so there is no need to raise your voice in du'a.
dalil.translation: Whatever you may say aloud, He knows what you keep secret and what is even more hidden.

dalil.context: There is no god but Allah, who has the most beautiful names. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: God––there is no god but Him––the most excellent names belong to Him.

dalil.context: Allah begins the story of Musa AS that Umar read. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Has the story of Moses come to you [Prophet]?

dalil.context: Musa AS saw a fire and went to look for directions, but was guided to Allah. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: He saw a fire and said to his people, ‘Stay here––I can see a fire. Maybe I can bring you a flaming brand from it or find some guidance there.’

dalil.context: Allah chose Musa and told him to listen to the revelation. Umar read this verse as if he himself were chosen.
dalil.translation: I have chosen you, so listen to what is being revealed.

dalil.context: Allah declares that he is Allah, there is no god but him, and orders worship and prayer to remember him. This is the verse that struck Umar.
dalil.translation: I am God; there is no god but Me. So worship Me and keep up the prayer so that you remember Me.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions this du'a as Umar reads Surah Ta-Ha and is moved by Allah's words choosing him.
dalil.translation: O Allah, strengthen Islam with whichever of the two men is most beloved to you, Umar ibn al-Khattab or Amr ibn Hisham.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions it as the narration of Ibn Abbas found in books of tafsir.
dalil.translation: When Umar accepted Islam, Jibril came down and said: O Muhammad, the people of heaven are glad at the Islam of Umar.

dalil.context: Shows the great effect of Umar's conversion on the Muslims' position in Mecca.
dalil.translation: We have been strong and honoured since the day Umar accepted Islam. We also never prayed openly in front of the Kaaba until Umar accepted Islam.

dalil.context: The ustaz links it to Umar's change from someone feared to a defender of Islam.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said that when Umar walks along one road, Satan takes another.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions it to show Umar's high standing, and that someone who was once far away can become very noble.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said that if there were a prophet after him, it would surely be Umar.

sirah.era: The Meccan phase, after the first migration to Abyssinia
sirah.summary: After the Quraysh envoys returned from Abyssinia having failed, the pressure on the Prophet ﷺ rose, and then Hamzah and later Umar accepted Islam and strengthened the Muslims' position in Mecca.

events.label: Abu Jahal's threat
events.title: Abu Jahal backs away from the Prophet ﷺ in prostration
events.desc: After swearing to tread on the Prophet's ﷺ neck, Abu Jahal retreated because he saw something frightening.

events.label: Hamzah and Abu Jahal
events.title: Hamzah strikes Abu Jahal
events.desc: On hearing that Abu Jahal had insulted the Prophet ﷺ, Hamzah struck his head with an arrow and declared himself on the Prophet's religion.

events.label: Hamzah accepts Islam
events.title: Hamzah prays and accepts Islam
events.desc: That night Hamzah was restless and prayed for Allah to show him the truth, then declared the shahada before the Prophet ﷺ the next day.

events.label: Umar sets out
events.title: Umar sets out with a sword
events.desc: Umar walked out to kill the Prophet ﷺ but was told by Nu'aym to look at his own family.

events.label: Fatimah's house
events.title: Umar strikes his sister and is moved
events.desc: Umar struck Sa'id and Fatimah, but seeing his sister's blood made him ashamed and he asked for the sheets they were reading.

events.label: Surah Ta-Ha
events.title: Umar bathes and reads Surah Ta-Ha
events.desc: Umar bathed to calm himself, then read Surah Ta-Ha up to the words in which Allah chose him, which shook his heart.

events.label: Dar al-Arqam
events.title: Umar accepts Islam
events.desc: Umar reached Dar al-Arqam with his sword, the Prophet ﷺ gripped his collar, and Umar declared the shahada.

events.label: Praying openly
events.title: The Muslims go out to pray at the Kaaba
events.desc: According to a sirah book the ustaz mentions, Hamzah and Umar walked in two lines to the Kaaba, and the Quraysh could do nothing.
